v1.22.0 is the release where the stack runs without an AWS account. Object storage, the graph
registries and mail each have a server of their own that the compose stack brings up, the
per-container memory caps read from `.env`, and a new technical page describes the shape between
a laptop and a cloud account: one machine on your own network, reached by the others through a
hostname, a certificate and one open port. Around that, the 1.21 series fixed what a sweep of the
demos found in the statements and the group close, took SEC tickers from EDGAR's current map, and
warmed shared replicas before they enter service.

Covers everything since v1.21.0; the 1.21.x patches carried generated changelogs.

## Running it yourself

**Object storage and the graph registries without AWS.** SeaweedFS replaces LocalStack as the
S3-compatible server of the development stack, on a Docker volume, so uploaded files, documents,
exports and graph backups survive a restart of the container and of the machine. DynamoDB Local
holds the graph registries on a volume of its own. A one-shot `storage-init` container creates the
buckets, their CORS rules and the registry tables only when they are missing and leaves existing
ones alone, so nothing is wiped on a start. The settings are botocore's per-service
`AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3` and `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_DYNAMODB`, each falling back to the global
`AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`; `AWS_S3_PRESIGN_ENDPOINT_URL` names the host a browser reaches when it differs
from the one the API uses. The backup adapter signs its download links with SigV4 and signs them
for that browser-reachable host. CI runs the same SeaweedFS image, and `awscli-local` is gone from
the development dependencies. A `.env` that set `LOCALSTACK_MEMORY_LIMIT` drops it;
`SEAWEEDFS_MEMORY_LIMIT`, `DYNAMODB_MEMORY_LIMIT` and `MAILPIT_MEMORY_LIMIT` take its place.

**Mail over SMTP.** Setting `SMTP_HOST` sends every email the platform writes, from verification
to invitations, over SMTP instead of Amazon SES: `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` and
`SMTP_STARTTLS` complete the setting, port 465 is implicit TLS, and any other port negotiates
STARTTLS unless told not to. The templates and the callers do not change, and a failed send is
still logged and reported rather than raised. The development stack gets Mailpit as its inbox: SMTP
on 1025, every message readable at `http://localhost:8025`, and the stack points at it by default.

**Memory caps from `.env`.** Each container's memory cap interpolates a `*_MEMORY_LIMIT` variable
with the former value as its default, and the OpenSearch JVM heap takes `OPENSEARCH_JAVA_OPTS`
the same way, so a smaller machine lowers the caps without editing `compose.yaml`. The
`.env.example` block lists them with a set for a 16 GB machine.

**Self-Hosting on a Server.** A new technical page covers the published images and a pinned tag,
where the data lives, a hostname and a certificate with a Caddy example, users and API keys over
the API alone, MCP clients on laptops, and what still takes work by hand. `SSL_CERT_FILE` is
documented for host scripts behind a private certificate authority, since Python trusts the named
bundle instead of the machine's keychain. The self-hosted model page notes that the model server
can be another machine on your network, serving the operators and an MCP client at once.

**CloudWatch on a development stack.** The two metric publishers in the graph infrastructure
monitor that still reached for CloudWatch on a `dev` stack now skip it, as the other three already
did.

## The close and the statements

A sweep of the rebuilt demos found statements failing checks on books that are right, and the
group close describing itself in identifiers.

- **Statement checks that failed correct books are fixed.** The balance sheet identity
  `Assets = Liabilities + StockholdersEquity` failed every month of a group with outside owners by
  exactly their interest, because that equity sits beside `StockholdersEquity`; the rule is retired
  in favour of the rollup of `LiabilitiesAndEquity`, and the net income rollup no longer runs on
  the cash flow and equity statements, which carry the outside owners' share without continuing
  operations. The net income check also skipped a line that followed a deeper row, so a parent
  whose accounts net to zero made a correct statement fail; a line now counts for what the rows
  under it do not already cover.
- **Filed statements and the live ones agree again**, and the consolidated equity statement in an
  acquisition month shows the acquired capital as a movement rather than a dividend no one paid.
- **The consolidated cash flow no longer shows a non-cash acquisition** in the month a member is
  sold, and three breaks in the forecast the Plan page reads are fixed.
- **Cash flow rows are worded for the cash effect they show.** A rise in receivables reads as a
  decrease in cash, a gain on a disposition reads as a gain, and only the paired words those rows
  use are swapped, so a tenant's own label is left alone.
- **The consolidation engine speaks in the close's words.** Concepts by label rather than local
  name, a pending entry by its own memo, and every amount in dollars.

## Connections

- **One live QuickBooks row decides the write policy.** The write-back resolver and the shadow
  ledger both read the same live row, so a connect attempt still in OAuth can no longer stand in
  for the connection. A disconnect keeps the policy, so reconnecting never turns `shadow` back into
  write-back. `write_policy` on a connection now describes all three values: `qb_authoritative`,
  `shadow` and `native`.
- **`execute-event-block` is scoped to the group parent's books**, the rule the close and the
  outbox preview already applied; an event on a subsidiary's books is refused before any lookup.

## Graph fleet

- **Shared replicas warm before they enter service.** The warmup runs the typed tools' own query
  shapes for a configured set of filers through the pool's connections, so the engine's buffer pool
  fills and not only the OS cache, with its budget capped under the health wait. The monthly secret
  rotation leaves the replicas out of its service refresh, since nothing on a replica's query path
  uses the rotated credentials.
- **The local Dagster daemon mounts `migrations/` and `frameworks/` from the checkout**, so a
  database ahead of the image no longer crash-loops the daemon with a revision it cannot find.

## Billing

- **A Link or bank-account default is a payment method.** Listing a customer's methods filtered
  to cards, so a customer whose saved method was Link could create a first graph through Checkout
  and never a second through the create path.
- **The unused-time credit on an immediate graph deletion lands at once**, finalized at cancel
  rather than an hour later, and refunds the smaller unused share of time and AI credits, so an
  allocation spent on day one is not refunded as if it were untouched.

## SEC

- **Filer tickers come from EDGAR's current map**, in the catalog and then in the graph, with old
  tickers still resolving. Filers that listed after their first snapshot appear, and a filer whose
  ticker changed is found under its current one.
- **Thirteen filers dropped from the public catalog since September are back.** A placeholder
  entity row, written when a combined filing names a filer the graph had not met, could replace the
  row that knew the filer; the catalog now takes the row from the latest partition.
- **The filer catalog runs on demand** rather than on Spot, after Spot refused its launches for a
  week. The dataset card names the dump file `.lbdb`.

## Operations and streams

- **Runs submitted without an operation store no events**, which the mail-sending routes always
  intended, and in-process events go out on the operation stream under their wire names, so a
  client listening by name hears a queued streaming query complete.
- **The burst limiter recognizes an OAuth bearer on graph routes**, so an MCP call over OAuth is
  metered against its caller rather than the anonymous per-address bucket.
- **Stream sign-ins that use the token query parameter are marked in the audit log**, ahead of
  retiring that door; the TypeScript client stopped using it in 2.36.0.
- **The extensions GraphQL endpoint is served over HTTP only.** The schema has no subscriptions,
  and the WebSocket route the router added is removed.

## Infrastructure

- DuckDB moves to 1.5.6, inside its supported window after 1.4's ends on 2026-11-17.
- `uv` resolves with a 7-day release cooldown, `setup-uv` moves to v10.3.3, the monthly schedules
  move off the hour, and the production AMI pin retries.
- The lock carries `robosystems-client` 2.35.1, whose file upload keeps the signed `Host` header
  when `s3_endpoint_url` rewrites the upload URL. `just pg-mcp` launches the read-only Postgres MCP
  through a tunnel, and `just bastion-stop` turns the bastion off.
- Dependency bumps: joserfc, pypdf, pyasn1, sse-starlette, pytest-asyncio, and the actions groups.
- Migrations run on the orchestrator's boot: on the extensions database, the retirement of the
  balance sheet identity rule and its false failures.
- The shared-replica CloudFormation template carries the warmup budget; the stack is updated by a
  deploy from a release before v1.21.2.

A deployment on v1.21.12 restarts into this release with no manual step. A self-hosted stack moving
from LocalStack replaces `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` in `.env` with the two per-service settings, removes the
old container and its volume, and starts; the `storage-init` container creates what the new stores
need on the first start.
